reviewMethod: Complete archived-source drafting followed by separate complete-source editorial review. Chapter coverage is accounted for in the inventory.

headings.title: Employing an attorney and setting compensation
headings.reviewNote: Collector authority is tied to141.010–141.160; the stated monthly compensation cap concerns first-class counties using those provisions exclusively.

headings.title: Salary coverage and combined-law compensation
headings.reviewNote: Salary replaces other fees for the stated services; counties operating both these sections and the land tax collection law instead compensate under that law. Does not apply the subsection1 cap universally.

entries.reviewSummary: Read both subsections/history. Exclusive firstclass collection-law salary300cap differs combinedlandtaxlaw compensation; servicesreplacefees retained.

headings.title: Employing abstracters and filing certified title memoranda
headings.reviewNote: Applies to the stated first-class counties with charter government enforcing liens by real-estate suit; covers all recorded conveyances, liens and charges, filing with petition, and eventual purchaser ownership of the abstracts.

headings.title: Abstract fees as litigation costs
headings.reviewNote: Covers the per-abstract ceiling and treatment of compensation as costs, without describing it as a general title-search price limit.

entries.reviewSummary: Read both subsections/history. Firstclassnoncharter exception, certifiedconveyance/lien abstracts filedwithpetition and purchaserproperty, ten-dollarcap litigationcost retained.

headings.title: Optional contributions of taxes on ancillary parcels
headings.reviewNote: Taxing authorities may contribute all or part of received tax distributions when the acquired ancillary parcel is encumbered by their tax lien or claim.

headings.title: Remitting tax-lien payments and credits through the collector
headings.reviewNote: Covers the agency’s duty concerning amounts attributable to taxing-authority real-property liens or claims; does not treat its optional contribution as eliminating the remittance requirement.

entries.reviewSummary: Read both subsections/history. Ancillaryparceltaxlien context, taxingauthorityoptional contribution of receivedtaxes, agencyremittanceofattributablepayments/credits retained.

headings.title: Land-bank authority and standing to quiet title
headings.reviewNote: Authority concerns real property in which the agency has an interest, with sufficient legal, equitable and possessory interests specified for the action.

headings.title: Title examination and notice to interested parties
headings.reviewNote: All five notice methods read: recorded identities by registered/certified mail, occupied-property occupant mail, posting, newspaper and court/due-process methods. This version says prevailing notions, distinct from wording in140.1009.

headings.title: Affidavit identifying interests and notice methods
headings.reviewNote: Affidavit identifies all potentially interested parties and the form of notice provided, not only parties actually appearing.

headings.title: Hearing schedule and judgment on unanswered matters
headings.reviewNote: Ninety-day hearing scheduling and120-day final judgment are distinct; the latter applies only to matters without an interested party’s answer.

headings.title: Joining parcels in one quiet-title petition
headings.reviewNote: Allows one or more parcels in a single petition, without expanding subject matter or eliminating notice.2026severability note preserved.

entries.reviewSummary: Read all five subsections/allservice methods/2026notes. Interestbasedstanding, titleexamination, occupiedmail/posting/publication/courtmeans, affidavit and90dayhearing/120dayunansweredjudgment preserved; exactmunicipalitypublication differschapter140 wording.

headings.title: Conditional sale announcement, reporting, and appraisal
headings.reviewNote: Sheriff announces court approval condition and reports bid; court appoints two disinterested competent appraisers of property and improvements.

headings.title: Confirmation when bids exceed half the value
headings.reviewNote: Source uses exceeds fifty percent, not at least; do not fill the exact-equality gap by inference. Powell annotation concerning inadequacy of consideration remains visible.

headings.title: Confirmation considering superior tax liens
headings.reviewNote: Applies when the bid is below half the appraised value but combined with superior tax liens exceeds half; does not count all debts or any liens.

headings.title: Bid increases or disapproval below the threshold
headings.reviewNote: Court may request increase to half the appraisal when bid plus prior tax liens is less; acceptance and payment lead to approval, refusal to disapproval and continued judgment lien. Preserve distinct strict comparisons.

entries.reviewSummary: Read all four subsections/Powellnote. Courtconditionalapproval/twodisinterestedappraisers, strictabovehalf and belowhalfwithsuperiorlien provisions, bidincrease alternative; no invented rule at exacthalf, annotation notgeneralized to negate procedures.

headings.title: General tax law and charter-county election of chapter 140
headings.reviewNote: Applies compatible general law to first-class charter counties and permits a legislative ordinance electing chapter140 procedures.

headings.title: Additional collection fee in qualifying charter counties
headings.reviewNote: The five-percent fee is limited to charter counties above600000 inhabitants, added to the bill, paid by the taxpayer and deposited into county general fund.

headings.title: Chapter 140 procedures for first-class noncharter counties
headings.reviewNote: Excludes those counties from141.010–141.160 and directs use ofchapter140; does not extend the exclusion to all ofchapter141.

entries.reviewSummary: Read three subsections/history. Inconsistencyqualification, chartercounty ordinanceoption, over600000fivepercentfee and mandatorychapter140noncharterfirstclass route retained. Added missing spaces in chapter references.

headings.title: Personal-tax debts in first-class charter counties
headings.reviewNote: Includes the historical January1,1946 assessment/delinquency scope and personal-judgment remedy, while excluding first-class noncharter counties.

headings.title: Collection suits, certified tax bills, and costs
headings.reviewNote: Covers parties, multiple delinquent years in one count, prima facie certified-bill proof, applicable civil procedure and appeal rules, and no costs against listed public entities.

headings.title: Delinquency, suit periods, and debtor-estate claims
headings.reviewNote: This version uses January after delivery of bills to collector, April commencement and five years; do not import140.730’s February/three-year scheme. Also includes deceased and insolvent estate claims.

entries.reviewSummary: Read three subsections/history. Firstclasscharter scope, certifiedbill prima facie/civilcostlimits, Januarydelinquency and April/five-year suit timing distinctfrom140.730February/three-year, estates retained.

headings.title: Tax-attorney employment under the land tax collection law
headings.reviewNote: For first-class counties governed by141.210–141.810, covers duties collecting delinquent tangible personal-property taxes and salary in lieu of fees with the stated annual cap.

headings.title: Assistant attorneys and other collection staff
headings.reviewNote: Additional hiring and pay require county-commission approval and include clerical and other necessary assistants.

headings.title: Attorney compensation outside the land tax collection law
headings.reviewNote: For specified first-class charter counties not adopting that law, covers combined personal/real-estate collection representation and the separate salary cap; not the same coverage as subsection1.

entries.reviewSummary: Read three subsections/history. Participatinglandtaxlaw6500salary versus nonparticipatingcharter3600salary, feeinlieu and countyapproval assistants retained.

headings.title: County adoption of the land tax collection law
headings.reviewNote: County election is by commission resolution or order and refers specifically to141.210–141.810.

headings.title: Partial county adoption and parcel selection
headings.reviewNote: After county adoption as partial opt-in, collector may elect the procedure parcel by parcel; not automatic conversion of all parcels.

headings.title: Land-bank prerequisite for qualifying partial opt-in counties
headings.reviewNote: The prerequisite is limited to counties eligible under140.981(1), not every county choosing partial adoption.

headings.title: Filing certified copies of the adoption action
headings.reviewNote: Ten-day filing covers county clerk and collector plus specified municipal officials; label does not imply filing only at county level.

headings.title: Municipal cooperation and rescinding county adoption
headings.reviewNote: Includes cooperation, a year before rescission can be adopted, another year before rescission takes effect, preservation of pending proceedings and treatment of earlier participating counties.

headings.title: Municipalities spanning participating county boundaries
headings.reviewNote: Cooperation applies to municipalities partly in the county, but taxes on out-of-county property follow other law; no extraterritorial collection power implied.

entries.reviewSummary: Read full six subsections/2026notes. Optionalwhole orpartial countyadoption, eligiblelandbankfirst, ten-daycopies, waitoneyearbefore rescission plusoneyear effectiveness and ongoingforeclosure preserved, outsidecounty municipalparcels excluded retained.

headings.title: Equal general-tax liens and priority by year
headings.reviewNote: Same-year listed governmental general-tax liens are equal first liens; newer unpaid years outrank older years, not the reverse.

headings.title: Priority of nongeneral-tax liens
headings.reviewNote: These liens are junior to general-tax liens; among themselves newer issues outrank older ones.

headings.title: Allocating proceeds by lien rank and amount
headings.reviewNote: Senior liens receive priority and equal-ranked liens share in proportion to their amounts; does not promise full payment to all.

entries.reviewSummary: Read three subsections/notes. Sameyear general taxliens equal, newer senior, nongeneraljunior and neweramongthose, equalrankprorata distribution retained.

headings.title: Foreclosure of tax liens after two years
headings.reviewNote: General-tax timing runs from delinquency and special-tax timing from the bill or installment due date.2004HousingAuthority annotation limits availability for involuntary special-assessment liens; title is a topic, not unconditional eligibility.

headings.title: Uncancelled tax instruments as evidence of nonpayment
headings.reviewNote: Covers ownership of listed instruments without evidence of payment or cancellation as prima facie, not conclusive, evidence of nonpayment.

headings.title: Municipal tax-certificate holders’ priority and foreclosure rights
headings.reviewNote: Covers holders of municipal tax sale certificates, purchase certificates or tax deeds at parity with same-year general-tax authorities; preserve the housing-authority source annotation.

entries.reviewSummary: Read three subsections and HousingAuthority2004annotation. Two-year generaldelinquency/specialdue trigger, uncancelledinstrument prima facie and municipalcertificate sameyear parity retained; annotation exception not presented as universally available foreclosure.

headings.title: Annual lists of parcels with delinquent tax liens
headings.reviewNote: January5 filing concerns parcels with liens delinquent at least two years and includes delinquent bills for all years, subject to subsection3’s exemption.

headings.title: Per-parcel filing fees and their collection
headings.reviewNote: Covers the specified filing fee paid to collector, charged against the parcel and accounted as costs.

headings.title: Exemption for collector-collected taxing authorities
headings.reviewNote: School districts and other authorities whose taxes must be collected by collector do not file lists or pay the filing fee; not an exemption from taxes or liens.

headings.title: Including younger liens on qualifying parcels
headings.reviewNote: Where any authority’s taxes are two or more years delinquent, other listed liens are included even if themselves newer; distinguishes parcel qualification from each lien’s age.

entries.reviewSummary: Read four subsections/notes. January5two-yearparcels with all delinquentyears,1.50parcelcost, collector-requiredtax exemption and youngerlien inclusion if anyqualifying taxes retained.

headings.title: Combining delinquent-tax lists
headings.reviewNote: Collector combines delinquent state, county, school and other collectible bills with lists from other authorities and bill owners.

headings.title: Selecting parcels in partial opt-in counties
headings.reviewNote: Collector chooses parcels proceeding under this chapter; remaining parcels follow other applicable provisions.

headings.title: Parcel identifiers and consolidation of pending suits
headings.reviewNote: Covers serial numbers, docket and court designations, and automatic consolidation/abatement of listed pending suits into the specified statutory proceeding.

headings.title: Delivering combined lists to the tax attorney
headings.reviewNote: Delivery may occur from time to time but no later than April1 each year.

headings.title: Preparing and filing foreclosure petitions
headings.reviewNote: Tax attorney incorporates lists in the141.410form and files by June1; distinct from the collector’s April delivery deadline.

entries.reviewSummary: Read all five subsections and 2026 severability note. Collector chooses partial-opt-in parcels; pending suits automatically consolidated and abated, April list delivery and June petition deadlines remain distinct. Titles unchanged.

headings.title: Receipts for listed delinquent tax bills
headings.reviewNote: Receipt states the aggregate listed amount and is held by the bill owner or appropriate taxing-authority financial officer.

headings.title: Monthly collection reports, remittances, and credits
headings.reviewNote: Includes affidavit-verified statements by the fifth, payment net of commissions/county costs by the fifteenth, and full-bill credits for specified land-trust and land-bank acquisitions.

entries.reviewSummary: Read both subsections and 2026 severability note. Aggregate receipts, fifth-day verified statements versus fifteenth-day net remittances, and specified land-trust/land-bank credits retained. Titles unchanged.

headings.title: Collector authority and suits by other lienholders
headings.reviewNote: Describes exclusive collection authority with an alternative when collector fails to sue in a year; other authorities or owners sue in collector’s name and provide petition ten days before filing.

headings.title: Advancing suit expenses and the collector-funded exception
headings.reviewNote: The bringing party generally advances costs, except specified same-parcel general-tax liens delinquent at least two years shift advances to collector. Source note records original-rolls word or rather than of; preserved.

entries.reviewSummary: Read both subsections and original-rolls note. Collector exclusivity after suit, other holder route on failure to sue with ten-day advance copy, and two-year general-tax condition for collector-advanced costs retained. Original or/of discrepancy not repaired. Titles unchanged.

headings.title: Appointing a tax attorney or designating county counsel
headings.reviewNote: Collector chooses appointed attorney or, where available, county counselor and needed assistants; no mandatory outside attorney is implied.

headings.title: Approved assistants, clerical employees, and expenses
headings.reviewNote: A tax attorney who is not county counselor may appoint with collector approval and incur necessary reasonable expenses.

headings.title: Collector representation and limits on other clients
headings.reviewNote: Covers collection litigation and expressly prohibits the attorney and collector from legal services for land trusts or land-bank agencies; not a general restriction on all government representation.

headings.title: County payment when designated funds are insufficient
headings.reviewNote: Monthly salary/expense payment for non-counselor attorney and staff comes from the stated treasury funds when cross-referenced funding is inadequate.

headings.title: Total compensation for appointed attorneys and staff
headings.reviewNote: Applies to the tax attorney who is not county counselor and the attorney’s assistants/employees; does not impose the same rule on every lawyer in the county.

headings.title: Quarterly verified compensation and expense returns
headings.reviewNote: Non-counselor attorney reports received compensation, amounts owed and staff salaries/expenses to county commission with affidavit verification.

headings.title: Attorney fees taxed and collected as suit costs
headings.reviewNote: Identifies statutory treatment of fees without inventing an amount or extending it beyond the suit.

entries.reviewSummary: Read seven subsections and 2026 severability note. Appointment/counsel designation options and approval, non-counsel qualifications for salary/returns, county fallback funds, and prohibition on land-trust/land-bank legal services retained. Titles unchanged.

headings.title: Consolidating pending suits and carrying forward liens
headings.reviewNote: Includes answer requirement generally and exception where bills are included in the collector petition, pending-suit abatement, and preservation of listed charges and liens.

headings.title: Preserving existing rights and defenses after consolidation
headings.reviewNote: Limitation statutes do not prevent assertion of rights/defenses already held in the pending actions; does not abolish every limitation period.

headings.title: Asserting existing liens and refiling dismissed claims
headings.reviewNote: Covers preexisting liens, inclusion or answer, a three-year action requirement if collector brings none, and one-year refiling after erroneous dismissal without prejudice.

entries.reviewSummary: Read all three subsections and history. List inclusion abates pending suit and excuses answer, existing rights/defenses retained, three-year action period differs from one-year dismissed-claim refiling. Titles unchanged.

headings.title: In-rem proceedings and permitted pleadings
headings.reviewNote: The statutory suit is in rem and pleadings consist of petition and answers; heading does not characterize it as a personal money-judgment action.

headings.title: Who may answer and what answers include
headings.reviewNote: Includes bill-interest and real-estate-interest claimants, nature and amount, defenses or objections, and optional cross/intervening allegations.

headings.title: Answer contents, service, and filing deadline
headings.reviewNote: Covers concise pleadings liberally construed, case/parcel identifiers, clerk filing and service on attorney within sixty calendar days after first publication, with Sunday/legal-holiday extension.

headings.title: Failure to answer and potential default judgments
headings.reviewNote: Petition is taken as confessed and default may be taken for unanswered parcels; title preserves may rather than promising automatic final judgment.

entries.reviewSummary: Read four subsections and history. In-rem scope, eligible interests and answer contents, sixty-day first-publication deadline with stated Sunday/holiday extension, and permissive default judgments retained. Titles unchanged.

headings.title: Filing foreclosure petitions and identifying interested persons
headings.reviewNote: Covers the circuit-clerk petition, caption, collector list and prayer, plus naming legal-interest holders reasonably discoverable from public records.

headings.title: Prescribed caption for the in-rem foreclosure petition
headings.reviewNote: Read the complete caption naming collector as plaintiff and encumbered land parcels as defendants; do not recast it as a personal action against owners.

headings.title: Required parcel and tax information
headings.reviewNote: All six categories read: petitioner/collector identity, street address, full legal description, tax ID, delinquency period and principal plus interest, penalties and fees.

headings.title: Requested foreclosure, priorities, sale, and further proceedings
headings.reviewNote: Prayer seeks lien foreclosure, amounts/priorities, sheriff sale and report for further proceedings under the cited provisions; not an automatic sale on filing.

headings.title: Notifying those who filed delinquent-tax lists
headings.reviewNote: Tax attorney sends registered notice within ten days identifying filing time/place and publication newspaper; this is distinct from notice to owners and occupants.

headings.title: Separate-suit effect for each listed parcel
headings.reviewNote: One petition has the same effect for each described parcel as an individual foreclosure suit.

entries.reviewSummary: Read six subsections, complete prescribed caption, nested information requirements and 2026 severability note. Reasonably discoverable interests, parcel/tax details, requested priority/sale relief, ten-day registered list-filer notices and separate-parcel suit effect retained. Titles unchanged.

headings.title: Redemption before the sheriff’s foreclosure sale
headings.reviewNote: Covers interested persons and payment of all listed amounts, with the express141.520(3) exception preserved; not a claim that there are no timing exceptions.

headings.title: Foreclosure of interests after failure to redeem
headings.reviewNote: Describes the subsection’s consequence at the foreclosure sale without erasing subsection1’s cross-referenced exception.

headings.title: Redemption certificates and collector records
headings.reviewNote: Redeemer receives certificate with petition-matching description, and collector records redeemed status and date.

headings.title: Redemption notice, lien release, and suit dismissal
headings.reviewNote: Collector notifies authority and tax attorney; payment releases and dismisses only the affected tax bills, not necessarily every parcel in a combined suit.

entries.reviewSummary: Read four subsections and history. Redemption includes charges and cross-referenced exception; failure before sheriff sale, certificate/record, prompt notices and bill-specific release/dismissal retained. Titles unchanged.

headings.title: Publishing the foreclosure notice
headings.reviewNote: Covers four successive weekly insertions on the same weekday in a legally qualified daily county newspaper after filing.

headings.title: Prescribed foreclosure notice and explanation of rights
headings.reviewNote: Entire long form read: in-rem character and federal-lien exception, parcel/bill information, answer and redemption rights, default warning, later redemption until sale, signatures and publication blanks. Original-rolls note on word in retained; title does not invent a different answer or redemption deadline.

entries.reviewSummary: Read both subsections and entire prescribed notice form, including all answer/redemption/default paragraphs and original-rolls in note. Four weekly publications, federal-lien exclusions in form, no personal judgment and redemption up to sale distinct from answer deadline retained. Titles unchanged.

headings.title: Tax-record and owner notices, returned mail and affidavits
headings.reviewNote: Covers thirty-day initial mail, addressee-only/return-receipt definition, successor-record search and remailing when returned other than refused, and affidavit at least thirty days before judgment describing failed or missing addresses.

headings.title: Mailing petition copies to property occupants
headings.reviewNote: First-class occupant copy is due within thirty days after filing, separate from the owner-notice methods in subsection1.

entries.reviewSummary: Read both subsections and 2026 severability note. Recipient includes last billed/charged person and different record owner, not only owners; revised first title accordingly. Defined restricted mail, search/remail for nonrefusal nondelivery, thirty-day pre-judgment affidavit and separate first-class occupant copy retained.

headings.title: Notice to representatives and guardian appointments
headings.reviewNote: Read the trigger for an infant, disabled person or confined convict answering or disability being raised; source specifies conservators, trustees and guardian-ad-litem alternatives. Do not silently infer an unrestricted representation right beyond the supplied wording.

headings.title: Appealing notice and representation failures
headings.reviewNote: After disability is raised, the failure is reviewable error but does not invalidate judgment absent appeal; a competent person may appeal on the protected party’s behalf.

entries.reviewSummary: Read both subsections and history. Disability/answer trigger, conservator/trustee notification or guardian appointment, reviewable error without automatic invalidation absent appeal, and competent-person appeal retained. Titles unchanged.

headings.title: Tax-bill evidence and pleading invalidity defenses
headings.reviewNote: Prima facie proof concerns assessment and nonpayment; absent answer allegations are confessed. Jurisdictional or invalidity defenses must be specified and affirmatively established, not presumed unavailable.

headings.title: Hearings, evidence, amounts, and lien priorities
headings.reviewNote: Includes optional informal issue clarification, attempted fact stipulation, amounts/interest accrual, tax-lien adjudication and other interests properly put in issue with service or appearance.

headings.title: Foreclosure judgments, sale outcomes, and continuing claims
headings.reviewNote: Entire long subsection read: validity/priority findings, redemption dismissal, exact-amount versus surplus sales, confirmation/appeal qualifications, distribution and surviving claims. Avoids a universal dismissal rule.

headings.title: Severance, appeals, and equitable bench trials
headings.reviewNote: Answer produces parcel-specific severance without delaying others; specified appeals do not stay tax foreclosure, trial is without jury, and precedence requires an interested party’s motion.

entries.reviewSummary: Read four complete lengthy subsections and history. Prima-facie tax bill and affirmative invalidity defense, optional informal hearings, required tax-lien versus optional other-interest adjudication, exact-payoff versus surplus distribution/continuing-claim paths, severance, unstayed specified appeals and equitable bench trial retained. Titles unchanged.

headings.title: Dismissal or foreclosure judgments and included amounts
headings.reviewNote: Includes absence-of-delinquency dismissal, evidence-dependent principal and charges, recited rates/fees and sale decree. Source’s fifteen-dollar language sits in a list of fees; label does not invent a cap covering all penalties or resolve its grammatical scope.

headings.title: Judgment notices and redemption-contract information
headings.reviewNote: Includes thirty-day owner notices, addressee-only mail, successor searches and remailing, and affidavit before confirmation hearings; notice also describes written-redemption-contract availability.

headings.title: Mailing foreclosure judgments to occupants
headings.reviewNote: Collector sends a first-class judgment copy within thirty days after judgment, distinct from owner notice and its return-receipt procedure.

entries.reviewSummary: Read all three subsections and2026severability note. Dismissal absent qualifying delinquency; neutral included-amounts title avoids resolving fifteen-dollar fee-cap grammatical scope. Thirty-day defined-mail notice, successor search and pre-confirmation affidavit, redemption-contract information and separate occupant judgment copy retained. Titles unchanged.

headings.title: Who may appeal and the appeal period
headings.reviewNote: Includes collector, any party, and anyone on behalf of a chapter475disabled person, with twenty days from foreclosure judgment.

headings.title: Appeal bonds and exempt appellants
headings.reviewNote: Collector, taxing authorities and appeals for disabled persons are exempt; other appellants need a court-approved bond securing diligent prosecution and resulting damages/costs including brief printing.

entries.reviewSummary: Read both subsections/history. Twenty-day appeal, collector/taxing-authority/disabled-person-representative bond exemptions versus court-approved bond for others, damages/cost conditions retained. Titles unchanged.

headings.title: Waiting before advertising the sheriff’s sale
headings.reviewNote: Six-month starting points differ after judgment, new-trial ruling or notice of appellate affirmance/mandate; subsection3 supplies an exception, so not an unconditional delay.

headings.title: Advertising and scheduling after the waiting period
headings.reviewNote: Preserves the source’s redemption/contract wording and rehearing/appeal timing; sale date falls within thirty days after first publication. Does not harmonize the or phrasing by inference.

headings.title: Vacant residential property: redemption and waiting-period exception
headings.reviewNote: Requires residential assessment and a judgment finding at least six months’ vacancy; after finality the stated redemption bar and immediate execution-sale procedure apply only to that category.

headings.title: Title searches in partial opt-in counties
headings.reviewNote: Licensed title company or attorney search of conveyances, liens and charges is due at least120days before sale for the specified judgments; cost may be recovered from proceeds.

headings.title: Locating interested parties through records and additional searches
headings.reviewNote: All five required record categories read, plus optional web-based searches and reasonable-cost recovery. Does not describe every supplemental search as compulsory.

headings.title: Mailed sale notices to interested parties
headings.reviewNote: First-class notice at least thirty days before sale identifies time/date/place and redemption cross-references; does not erase the separate vacant-property exception.

headings.title: Posting and documenting notices on the property
headings.reviewNote: Includes twenty-day timing, content, placement, dimensions/weatherproofing, removal prohibition, timestamped photograph, public availability and affidavit verification.

headings.title: Attempting and documenting in-person notice
headings.reviewNote: Requires an attempt at least twenty days before sale, permits notice to anyone found there, and documents attempt/person with affidavit. Does not promise completed personal service on an owner.

entries.reviewSummary: Read eight subsections, nested record searches and2026severability note. Six-month waiting/appeal events, vacant-residential judgment finding and redemption exception, partial-opt-in title search, thirty-day mail versus twenty-day posting and attempted in-person notice, photographs/affidavits/cost recovery retained. Attempt not misrepresented as completed service. Titles unchanged.

headings.title: Redemption contracts, installment limits, and discretionary extensions
headings.reviewNote: Includes141.520exception, optional monthly/bimonthly contract, general twelve-installment/twenty-four-month limits and good-cause court discretion for specified homestead or low-value income property up to forty-eight months.

headings.title: Extending the waiting period and installment defaults
headings.reviewNote: Timely contractual payments extend the wait; a missed installment ends the extension without notice and triggers advertising or inclusion in next sale notice.

entries.reviewSummary: Read both subsections/history. Cross-referenced exception, optional collector contract and normal twelve-installment/twenty-four-month limit, qualifying good-cause discretionary forty-eight-month extensions, continued waiting only while payments timely and default without notice retained. Titles unchanged.

headings.title: Staying tax sales during specified property actions
headings.reviewNote: Applies to447.620–447.640actions after pre-sale deposit of delinquent principal, with notice/certificate to court administrator; covers return of deposit if action dismissed before temporary possession.

headings.title: Deed orders, extinguished charges, and tax remittances
headings.reviewNote: Orders under447.625/.640extinguish listed penalties, interest, attorney fees and costs against grantee/successors and remit principal deposits to collector; not cancellation of all principal taxes.

headings.title: Owner restoration payments and repayment of earlier deposits
headings.reviewNote: Restoration motion requires all current taxes and retroactive charges; if owner regains possession, owner funds go to collector while initial action-bringer’s deposit is returned.

entries.reviewSummary: Read three subsections and2026severability note. Specified action plus principal deposit before sale and notice/certificate required; dismissal refund only before temporary possession, deed extinguishment versus owner-restoration full charges and payer reimbursement retained. Titles unchanged.

headings.title: Courthouse location of sheriff’s foreclosure sales
headings.reviewNote: Sale uses the courthouse front door customarily used for execution sales, within the stated county circumstances.

headings.title: Prescribed sheriff’s sale advertisement
headings.reviewNote: Complete form read, including grouped parcels, judgment amounts, public cash auction, land trust/bank provision, court confirmation and signature/date fields. No inference from form wording overrides the detailed sale statutes.

headings.title: Weekly publication before the sale
headings.reviewNote: Requires four successive weekly publications on the same weekday in a qualified daily county newspaper, distinct from the sale schedule itself.

entries.reviewSummary: Read three subsections, complete prescribed sale advertisement and2026severability note. Customary courthouse front door, public auction cash/highest bidder and confirmation in form, four weekly same-day publications retained. Titles unchanged.

headings.title: Execution-sale procedures and court-session independence
headings.reviewNote: General execution-sale procedure governs conduct, return and deed except statutory variations; sale need not be during court term or session.

headings.title: Sale schedule, minimum bids, and bidder eligibility
headings.reviewNote: All four subdivisions read: partial-opt-in August timing, charges that may differ from judgment plus nonreimbursable bidder fee, sewer-debt exclusion, county delinquency screening, registered agents and foreign authority. No single condition described as the only requirement.

headings.title: Code-violation screening in specified municipalities
headings.reviewNote: Population/geography qualification and two-violation demonstration preserved; taxing authorities and land banks are exempt from this demonstration, not necessarily all sale rules.

headings.title: Interests conveyed and retained utility and federal interests
headings.reviewNote: Whole interests transfer whether parties answered, subject to specified paid-tax utility rights-of-way and United States lien; title does not say unconditionally free of every lien.

headings.title: Advancing and allocating publication costs
headings.reviewNote: Collector advances/accounting credits and parcel allocation covered; enumerated costs do not remain liens after sale.

entries.reviewSummary: Read five subsections and all nested bidder criteria plus2026note. Partial-opt-in August date, actual taxes possibly different from judgment, nonrefundable200fee and sewer-debt exclusion; ten-day delinquency and registered-agent/authority screening; narrow municipal code test with governmental exception retained. Utility rights-of-way/federal lien and no publication-cost lien after sale retained. Titles unchanged.

headings.title: Daily adjournments and reoffering unsold parcels
headings.reviewNote: Applies when no bidders or inadequate time/opportunity, with same place/hour and announced reoffering.

headings.title: Deemed land-trust bids and cancellation of tax bills
headings.reviewNote: Applies outside wholly covered land-bank territory after three different offering days; preserves required public bid versus deemed judgment-based bid distinction, higher-bid qualification, confirmation and accounting.

headings.title: Deemed land-bank bids and cancellation of tax bills
headings.reviewNote: Applies to wholly covered territory after three offering days and confirmation. Does not copy the preceding subsection’s express no-higher-bid clause into this differently worded provision.

entries.reviewSummary: Read all three subsections and2026note independently. Three offerings need not be successive, outside/inside land-bank geography distinct. Trigger amount differs from deemed judgment-based bid; land-trust no-higher-bid clause is not supplied to land-bank text. Confirmation-dependent cancellation and credits retained. Titles unchanged.

headings.title: Confirmation hearings, notice findings, and quiet-title claims
headings.reviewNote: Includes hearing setting within six months, interested-party notice, value evidence and specific adequate-notice findings, plus preservation of purchaser’s quiet-title claim.

headings.title: Adequacy of consideration and conditional sale confirmation
headings.reviewNote: Read all alternatives: increased bid OR unpaid full tax judgment may permit confirmation; disapproval requires refusal to increase plus full payment by interested parties. Special land-trust/bank presumption is retained without treating price alone as decisive.

headings.title: Distribution priorities, surplus claims, and pending appeals
headings.reviewNote: All three priorities and continuation read, including land-bank exception to tax-bill distribution, other surplus issues, special-appeal custody and pro-rata shortfalls by class.

headings.title: Unclaimed sale proceeds after two years
headings.reviewNote: Remaining funds go to appropriate taxing authorities unless partial opt-in county, where county school fund receives them; not immediate forfeiture after sale.

headings.title: Funding defense of notice-sufficiency claims
headings.reviewNote: County may allocate a portion of its own proceeds share; discretionary and limited to this defense purpose.

headings.title: Redemption deposits before post-deed challenges
headings.reviewNote: Interested parties other than the sheriff-sale purchaser must deposit the cross-referenced redemption amount before hearing a motion to set aside after deed issuance; not a prerequisite applied equally to the purchaser.

entries.reviewSummary: Read all six subsections, nested priority list and2026note. Six-month setting of hearing, notice/due-process finding, quiet-title claim; inadequate bid may still be confirmed absent full interested-party tax payment, disapproval requires purchaser refusal plus full payment. Land-bank tax-payment exception, pro-rata and appeal retention, two-year unclaimed destination difference, optional defense fund and purchaser exception to post-deed redemption deposit retained. Titles unchanged.

headings.title: Five-percent suit penalty upon petition filing
headings.reviewNote: Penalty is calculated on principal and imposed as costs due to collector upon filing, in addition to the other charges; not five percent of the entire judgment.

headings.title: Penalty funds, litigation expenses, and remaining balances
headings.reviewNote: Separate fund includes recovered penalties/costs, retains needed advances including staffing and notices, transfers remainder annually to land trust or retains it where no trust exists.

entries.reviewSummary: Read both subsections and2026note. Five-percent principal penalty due on petition filing; separate fund includes other recovered costs, retained expenses and January1 remainder to land trust or collector retention when none exists. Titles unchanged.

headings.title: Prorating costs among tax bills
headings.reviewNote: Includes publication and court costs, apportioned pro rata among bills rather than an invented equal parcel fee.

headings.title: Additional costs payable upon redemption
headings.reviewNote: All four fee items read, including distinct amounts triggered by begun publication and sheriff-sale notice and the clerk’s dismissal charge.

headings.title: Crediting costs and reimbursing advances
headings.reviewNote: Collector credits proper accounts and is reimbursed from costs for advances under the statutory procedures.

entries.reviewSummary: Read three subsections and four nested redemption charges/history. Pro-rata bill costs, event-dependent additional parcel charges and circuit-clerk payment, account credits and advance reimbursement retained. Titles unchanged.

headings.title: Exclusive collection procedures and partial opt-in exception
headings.reviewNote: Exclusivity for electing counties expressly excepts partial opt-in counties; conflict clause retained without claiming exclusivity statewide.

headings.title: Court judgment before selling parcels in pending petitions
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits authorities/bill owners from advertising or selling petition-included parcels absent a court judgment ordering it; does not impose the rule on all property in all contexts.

headings.title: Adding later tax claims before judgment
headings.reviewNote: Tax authority or bill owner may assert later-due taxes by amendment or answer, subject to court allowance; these are not automatically included.

entries.reviewSummary: Read three subsections and2026note. Partial-opt-in exception to exclusivity, court-judgment prerequisite only for parcels in pending petitions, optional later-tax claims before judgment subject allowance retained. Titles unchanged.

headings.title: Land-trust membership and appointing authorities
headings.reviewNote: Three positions derive from county and eligible largest municipality/school district, excluding specified land-bank appointing authorities; county fills failures after expired terms.

headings.title: Trustee terms and changes after land-bank establishment
headings.reviewNote: Includes four-year terms, historical initial appointment window and early termination tied to land-bank transfers or one year, whichever first.

headings.title: Residence, experience, and conflicting-office qualifications
headings.reviewNote: Includes five-year county residence, ten-year real-estate experience and prohibition on compensated public office whose duties conflict, not every other public role.

headings.title: Initial staggered terms and service until succession
headings.reviewNote: Preserves historical1946–1948expiration dates and holding office until successor appointment/qualification rather than applying those dates to new terms.

headings.title: Vacancies and county fallback appointments
headings.reviewNote: Original appointing authority fills unexpired term; county acts after specified initial appointment or thirty-day failures.

headings.title: Annual trustee salaries
headings.reviewNote: Neutral topic for the statutory annual salary, without assertion of a current adjusted compensation amount.

headings.title: Removal for cause and opportunity to be heard
headings.reviewNote: Includes respective appointing authority, public hearing if requested, counsel and evidence opportunity; hearing request qualification preserved.

entries.reviewSummary: Read seven subsections/history. Eligible appointing authorities exclude land-bank appointors, transition ends on earlier transfer completion/one year, experience/residence/conflicting-office qualifications, historical1946–1948 terms, fallback appointments and requested hearing/counsel retained. Titles unchanged.

headings.title: Selecting land-trust officers
headings.reviewNote: Initial meeting follows all three appointments and qualification; listed officers include an assistant secretary who need not be a trustee.

headings.title: Trustee surety bonds and county-paid premiums
headings.reviewNote: Includes stated ceiling, collector approval, licensed surety, county-clerk deposit and coverage of all trustees; not confused with commissioner’s minimum bond in141.740.

headings.title: Prescribed trustee oath before taking office
headings.reviewNote: Complete oath/form read including public-body and tax-bill-owner benefit, impartial duties, signatures and notarization; not an invented additional oath.

entries.reviewSummary: Read three subsections and complete sworn oath/history. Four offices with assistant secretary not necessarily trustee, each-furnish versus cover-all bond wording left unaltered, premium county advance and oath beneficiaries retained. Titles unchanged.

headings.title: Appointing staff and setting compensation and expenses
headings.reviewNote: Board may appoint commissioner, other employees and required attorneys, with salaries, benefits and reasonable related costs.

headings.title: Land commissioner’s bond
headings.reviewNote: Trust pays premium, trustees approve, amount has a minimum not the trustee-bond ceiling, and bond is filed with county clerk.

headings.title: Commissioner qualifications and executive responsibilities
headings.reviewNote: Requires real-estate management/sale experience; commissioner administers trust business under trustees’ supervision and control.

entries.reviewSummary: Read three subsections/history. Discretionary appointments and compensation, land-trust-paid minimum10000bond, experienced commissioner under trustee control retained. Titles unchanged.

headings.title: Land-trust corporate powers, seal, and deed execution
headings.reviewNote: Covers continuing body, official seal, suit/deed authority, specified signers and attestation, and general business administration.

headings.title: Conveyances, appraisal thresholds, and small-tract exception
headings.reviewNote: Includes warranty/fee conveyance without beneficiary instruments, deed recital of appraisal comparison, two appointing-authority consents below two-thirds, and limited contiguous-owner small-vacant-tract sale without appraisal.

entries.reviewSummary: Read both subsections/history. Deed signatures/attestation and corporate powers, appraisal two-thirds threshold and two appointor consents, narrow vacant-residential/contiguous-owner half-assessed-price exception retained. Titles unchanged.

headings.title: Annual budget preparation, approval, and carryover
headings.reviewNote: Read October1submission, November20deemed approval, prior-year fallback on January1when objections unresolved, and deduction of prior unexpended funds.

headings.title: Public budget access, hearings, and amendments
headings.reviewNote: Separate October10public copies and pre-October20hearing; amendments require appointing bodies’ approval.

headings.title: Expense advances, requisition limits, and county reimbursement
headings.reviewNote: Entire long formula read: county7percent, qualifying taxing bodies93percent, proportional base,25percent budget limit absent additional approval, county advance of other shares and reimbursement/withholding.

headings.title: Fiscal year, claim audits, and payment warrants
headings.reviewNote: January1fiscal start and trust audit of expenditure claims precede warrants drawn through chair or vice chair.

headings.title: Payment certifications, commissioner liability and removal
headings.reviewNote: Approval and certification of both appropriation balance and cash required; contrary certification entails personal/bond liability and removal.

headings.title: Performance audits and public availability
headings.reviewNote: Optional state or qualifying city audit supplements annual audit; trust pays and supplies copies within thirty days. Does not authorize any city auditor regardless of statutory class.

entries.reviewSummary: Read six complete subsections/history. October/November budget dates, deemed approval and prior-budget carryover, unexpended deduction,7/93allocation and25percent requisition ceiling with excess approval, county advances/reimbursement retained. Revised(5) to name certification liability and removal because contrary certification, not necessarily completed improper payment, triggers it. Narrow city auditor category and30-day public copies retained.

headings.title: Land-trust authority and standing to quiet title
headings.reviewNote: Applies to trust-held interests under527.150and deems adequate legal, equitable and possessory interests; distinct actor from land-bank provisions.

headings.title: Title examination and service on interested parties
headings.reviewNote: All five methods read, including occupied-property mailing, posting, publication and court-ordered methods; does not insert the additional due-process phrase from141.1009.

headings.title: Affidavit identifying interested parties and notice
headings.reviewNote: Identifies potentially interested parties and notice form, not merely recipients who answered.

headings.title: Hearings and judgment on unanswered matters
headings.reviewNote: Ninety-day hearing schedule and120-day judgment only for unanswered matters remain distinct.

headings.title: Joining parcels in one quiet-title petition
headings.reviewNote: Trust may join one or more parcels, without eliminating each parcel’s required notice.

entries.reviewSummary: Read five subsections/all five notice methods/history. Sufficient-interest standing, title examination and multiple notice routes, ninety-day hearing versus120-day judgment on unanswered matters, parcel joinder retained. Titles unchanged.

headings.title: Limits on trustees’ and employees’ property-related profits
headings.reviewNote: Covers direct/indirect compensation from trust-land transactions beyond provided salaries, expenses and emoluments; unlike141.819(5), this text expressly has an allowance.

headings.title: Criminal penalty for violating compensation restrictions
headings.reviewNote: Describes conviction-based felony sanction rather than asserting any payment automatically results in imprisonment.

entries.reviewSummary: Read both subsections/history. Trustees and salaried employees restricted except authorized salaries/expenses/emoluments; conviction-based felony penalty retained without broadening employee category. Titles unchanged.

headings.title: Creating partial opt-in land trusts and appointing trustees
headings.reviewNote: Before confirmation of the specified deemed bid, county establishes trust with one or three trustees; initial two/three-year and later two-year terms and unexpired vacancies preserved.

headings.title: No land trust when the county establishes a land bank
headings.reviewNote: Exclusion applies to county election under140.981(1) and the specified statutory trust span; not every municipal land bank.

headings.title: Property disposition votes and appraisal-based approval
headings.reviewNote: Trustee majority acts; below-two-thirds appraisal consideration requires county-commission majority, distinct from141.750two-appointing-authority consent.

headings.title: Operating accounts and distribution of disposition proceeds
headings.reviewNote: Both subdivisions read: operating accounts and order of sale expenses, listed property costs, then county general fund.

headings.title: Prohibition on trustee profits from trust-held land
headings.reviewNote: This version prohibits the listed compensation, emoluments or profits without141.810’s salary/expense allowance; do not import that exception.

entries.reviewSummary: Read five subsections/nested distribution order and2026note. Partial-opt-in trust before deemed-bid confirmation unless county land bank, one-or-three trustees and initial/subsequent terms, two-thirds threshold and county approval, expenses/property costs/general-fund priority and uncompromised trustee-profit prohibition retained. Titles unchanged.

headings.title: Municipal land-bank establishment, purpose, and eligibility
headings.reviewNote: Both subdivisions read: named act, municipality within wholly operating county, ordinance or resolution, return to private or public use, municipal boundary restriction, and exclusion of partial opt-in counties.

headings.title: Taxing-authority beneficiaries and proportional interests
headings.reviewNote: Identifies three specified acquisition routes and court-determined priorities and principal-tax-bill proportions; does not extend beneficiary treatment to every donated parcel.

headings.title: Public corporate status and duration until dissolution
headings.reviewNote: Permanent public body corporate and politic remains subject to termination and dissolution under141.1012; not an assertion that dissolution is impossible.

entries.reviewSummary: Read all three subsections, nested act/purpose provisions and2026severability note. Municipality in wholly operating county only, no partial-opt-in or outside-boundary ownership; beneficiaries tied to listed acquisition routes and court principal-based priorities; permanent duration subject dissolution retained. Titles unchanged.

headings.title: Board appointments, terms, vacancies, and appointing authorities
headings.reviewNote: Full five-member allocation, county and largest-population school district representation, municipal remainder, four-year terms, pleasure service, no compensation, sixty-day fallback appointments and141.720exception read.

headings.title: Eligibility of public officers and subdivision employees
headings.reviewNote: Elected political-subdivision officers may retain their offices while serving; employees are also eligible. Does not broaden the defined public officer to all offices.

headings.title: Annual selection of board officers and their duties
headings.reviewNote: Board chooses chair, vice chair, treasurer and other officers annually from members and establishes duties subject to board rules.

headings.title: Agency organization, personnel compensation, and expense reimbursement
headings.reviewNote: Board may reorganize departments and fix employees’, agents’ and consultants’ duties, powers and compensation; member reimbursement is for actual performance-related expenses.

headings.title: Regular and special meetings and quorum
headings.reviewNote: Board-adopted schedule, chairman or majority-signed special-session notice, and majority of total membership quorum all read.

headings.title: Voting requirements and matters requiring full-board majorities
headings.reviewNote: General present-and-voting majority differs from six listed matters requiring roll-call majority of entire membership; hiring delegation, low-price sales and fifty-thousand-dollar value threshold retained.

headings.title: Commissioner surety bonds and governmental coverage exception
headings.reviewNote: Bond requirement subject to existing governmental surety coverage, maximum penal sum, municipal approval, licensed surety, county deposit and faithful-performance/all-commissioner coverage.

headings.title: Commissioner oath before taking office
headings.reviewNote: Complete oath and notarial form read, including constitutional support, impartial administration of tax-delinquent and other lands, and represented public bodies and tax-bill owners.

headings.title: Protection from personal liability for agency obligations
headings.reviewNote: Members not personally liable on agency bonds or other obligations; creditors’ rights run solely to agency assets. Does not imply immunity for all individual misconduct.

headings.title: No proxy voting and requests for recorded votes
headings.reviewNote: Every member may request a recorded vote on a resolution or action; proxy voting prohibited.

entries.reviewSummary: Read ten subsections, six special voting matters, complete oath and history. Five-member allocation, appointor pleasure/no compensation and fallback, elected-officer definition, actual-expense reimbursements, ordinary versus full-board roll-call votes/delegable staffing, bond coverage exception and no personal agency-obligation liability retained. No proxy voting distinguished from recorded-vote request. Titles unchanged.

headings.title: Transfer of land-trust property within the municipality
headings.reviewNote: One-year deadline after establishing ordinance or resolution applies to land-trust real property wholly within the creating municipality, not all county trust land.

headings.title: Tax exemptions, ownership notices, and ground-lease occupancy
headings.reviewNote: Income exemption and ownership-period property exemption distinguished; immediate assessor/collector notices for acquisition, disposition and first occupancy that ends exemption for improved occupied ground-leased property.

headings.title: Property acquisition methods subject to municipal limits
headings.reviewNote: Gift, devise, transfer, exchange, foreclosure, purchase and other acquisition remain subject to141.980(1)rather than unrestricted statewide acquisition.

headings.title: Purchase contracts, public transfers, and foreclosure bidding
headings.reviewNote: Repeated141.980(1)limits, agreed public-transfer conditions,141.550sheriff-sale bidding and subdivision transfer procedures all read; source’s “land contacts” wording retained in body.

headings.title: Compliance with property maintenance laws and ordinances
headings.reviewNote: Agency must maintain all real property under laws and ordinances of the jurisdictions where it is located.

headings.title: Payment of excess bids and cancellation of tax bills
headings.reviewNote: Confirmed specified foreclosure-sale acquisition requires payment only of bid excess over listed judgment amounts, prescribed distribution excluding141.580(3)(3), and collector cancellation/credit of included bills and charges.

entries.reviewSummary: Read six subsections and2026severability note. One-year wholly municipal transfer; ownership notices, public-real-estate exemption and first ground-lease occupancy termination; municipal limits on acquisition and bidding, maintenance compliance and confirmed excess-bid payment/cancelled tax bills retained. Source land contacts wording not repaired. Titles unchanged.

headings.title: Holding acquired property in the agency’s own name
headings.reviewNote: Applies regardless of the transferor’s identity; no claim that agency title resolves all encumbrances.

headings.title: Public property inventory and required website information
headings.reviewNote: Inventory must be inspectable and online with sale availability, assigned address or unaddressed parcel number, and acquisition year.

headings.title: Policies on consideration for property transfers
headings.reviewNote: Consideration includes monetary/secured obligations, use covenants and conditions, transferee commitments and other board-determined forms; not necessarily cash or market value alone.

headings.title: Property transfer and encumbrance powers within statutory limits
headings.reviewNote: All conveyance, lease, pledge and related powers remain subject to141.980(1).

headings.title: Municipal priorities for conveyed property uses
headings.reviewNote: Optional priority hierarchy, listed public/affordable housing/commercial/wildlife uses, subsection7limit and consistency with/no greater restrictiveness than planning and zoning all read.

headings.title: Delegating execution of property conveyance documents
headings.reviewNote: Board may delegate officers/employees authority for agreements, conveyance instruments and related documents; not an unlimited delegation of all board powers.

headings.title: Fair-market-value offers and judicial review of rejection or delay
headings.reviewNote: Written offers at or above fair market value, sixty-day nonresponse, competing accepted qualifying offer exception and county venue read. Original-roll “is” note retained; no invented automatic transfer.

headings.title: Proceeds from specified tax-sale and land-trust acquisitions
headings.reviewNote: Three acquisition routes and ordered sale/financing/budget distributions distinguished from ancillary parcels; reasonable carryover, ancillary-profit exclusion, current taxing authorities’ levy proportions and January/July dates retained.

headings.title: Ancillary-parcel proceeds and payment priorities
headings.reviewNote: Land taxes and charges paid before sale costs, financing obligations and operating balance. Excess provision refers to subsection8(3), not8(4); preserves that reference without silently substituting taxing-authority distribution.

headings.title: Price reductions for unsold properties in the same block
headings.reviewNote: Mandatory discount and public advertisement require more than five owned parcels in a single block and no offer for any of them in preceding twelve months; not a general annual price cut.

entries.reviewSummary: Read all ten subsections, nested proceeds priorities and original-rolls note. Agency ownership and inventory, discretionary consideration/use priorities, mandatory fair-market-value offer path with pending accepted-offer exception, review after rejection or sixty days, three acquisition routes and distinct ancillary proceeds retained. Subsection 9 points to 8(3), not 8(4); did not repair that reference. Block price reduction requires more than five properties and twelve months without an offer. Titles unchanged.

headings.title: Grants and loans from public and private sources
headings.reviewNote: Agency may receive grants/loans from subdivisions, state, federal and other public/private sources.

headings.title: Retaining operating and asset income subject to distribution rules
headings.reviewNote: Service/rent/lease/disposition/insurance/investment and other lawful income are subject to141.985(8)and(9)exceptions.

headings.title: Post-disposition tax distributions, exclusions, and offsets
headings.reviewNote: Three tax years following sale, collected-not-refunded condition, fees/deductions, following March1deadline, protested/impounded-tax exclusion and erroneous-prior-distribution offsets all read.

headings.title: County fee on reserve-period tax collections
headings.reviewNote: Four-percent fee on reserve-period taxes is collected for and deposited in county general fund, additional to other collection-fee law.

entries.reviewSummary: Read all four subsections and history. Funding permissions distinguished from retained-income distribution exceptions; three post-disposition tax years, exclusions for protested/impounded and refunded taxes, fees, March deadline and erroneous-distribution offsets retained. Four-percent county reserve-period fee distinct from agency distribution. Titles unchanged.

headings.title: Municipally approved revenue bonds and security
headings.reviewNote: Special limited agency obligations require creating municipality’s approval, specified asset revenues and possible additional revenue pledges or property security; not general taxing-power bonds.

headings.title: Bond debt limitations, public liability, and personal liability
headings.reviewNote: Excludes constitutional/statutory indebtedness classification and state/subdivision liability subject to subsection4exception; required recital and issuance-related personal liability protection read.

headings.title: Board authorization, bond terms, and public or private sales
headings.reviewNote: Resolution and approved financing documents govern form, denominations, interest, maturity, redemption and execution; board selects sale method/price in agency’s interests.

headings.title: Optional political-subdivision guarantees and obligations
headings.reviewNote: Election to guarantee/insure or assume obligation remains subject to Missouri debt law; no obligation absent election.

headings.title: Refunding bonds for existing valid obligations
headings.reviewNote: Board-authorized refunding, extending and unifying valid outstanding bonds, identified revenue sources and investment proceeds; not all future expenditures.

headings.title: Negotiability under Missouri’s Uniform Commercial Code
headings.reviewNote: Applies negotiable-instrument treatment to bonds issued by the agency.

headings.title: State tax exemption with estate and transfer tax exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Bonds and income/interest exempt from state taxes except estate and transfer taxes; no assertion of federal exemption.

headings.title: Temporary notes and refunding authority
headings.reviewNote: Temporary notes carry bond terms/restrictions and may be refunded with authorized notes or bonds.

entries.reviewSummary: Read all eight subsections and history. Municipal approval, special limited revenue obligations and possible additional security preserved; general public-debt exclusion subject optional lawful political-subdivision guarantee, personal liability exclusion, board terms and public/private sale discretion checked. Refunding outstanding valid bonds, negotiability, estate/transfer tax exceptions and restricted temporary notes retained. Titles unchanged.
